topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture’s subject and establishes its objectives before the substantive discussion begins.

topics.label: Cancer as clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic establishes the biological model of cancer as an evolving clone within a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Sources of cancer risk and evidence for environmental influences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer risk is attributed to different causes and what evidence supports environmental contributions.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infection contributes to cancer development, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a specific example.

topics.label: Carcinogen-induced DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how particular carcinogenic exposures produce DNA damage through direct or indirect molecular mechanisms.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and tissue susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how tissue conditions influence the development of tumours after carcinogenic exposure and conclude by synthesising the mechanisms discussed.

topics.label: Exposure evidence and epidemiological assessment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological evidence of exposure supports the assessment of carcinogenicity in human populations.

topics.label: Experimental carcinogenicity testing and its limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess laboratory approaches to identifying carcinogenic potential and the limitations of interpreting their results.

topics.label: Lecture summary and risk–benefit conclusions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by reviewing its main findings and drawing together their implications for risk–benefit decisions.
